sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Receptor used in functional BRET-based G protein coupling assays in mammalian cells (PMC12006980); the FLAG-MRGPRD-Rluc8 construct was employed for functional assays, implying receptor activity was preserved.
sites.rationale: L5 reports a full-length human MRGPRD construct with an N-terminal FLAG tag used in functional assays. MRGPRD has no signal peptide and its N-terminus (residues 1-28) is extracellular per topology landmarks; this is the only extracellular terminus available for an N-terminal tag. Without a primer sequence, the junction is topology-derived as a prepend (insert_after_residue=0, before M at position 1). The extracellular N-terminus is 28 residues long, cysteine-free, and well clear of TM1 (>=3 residue constraint satisfied). Full-length human MRGPRD cloned into pcDNA3.1 with an N-terminal FLAG tag and C-terminal Rluc8 for functional BRET assays in mammalian cells (PMC12006980). No primer sequence is provided, so the exact junction cannot be pinned to a residue; 'N-terminal' on a GPCR with an extracellular N-terminus (residues 1-28, no signal peptide) and no other extracellular terminus available for a prepend places the tag before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0).

sources.claim: For the Gq protein, we used the same mini-GaqiN heterotrimer (referred to Gq hereinafter) construct that was firstly reported in the expression of HTR2A-Gq-NBOH complex. 24 For the functional assays, the human MRGPRD gene was cloned into the pcDNA3.1 vector containing an N-terminal FLAG tag with a C-terminal Rluc8 gene.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Receptor expressed and used for functional characterization (PMC2947157 describes expression and functional characterization of HA-tagged human MrgD); specific assay results not detailed in ledger clip.
sites.rationale: The forward PCR primer in L1 encodes M-YPYDVPDYA-NQTLNSS, where NQTLNSS matches residues 2-8 of canonical human MRGPRD (UniProt). Python decoding of the primer codons confirms the HA tag is inserted after M(1) and before N(2), placing it within the 28-residue extracellular N-terminus (topology landmarks 1-28), 27 residues from TM1. No cysteines or disulfide bonds are present in this region, and the junction is well clear of the TM boundary (>=3 residue constraint satisfied). Full-length human MrgD expressed in mammalian cells with HA tag inserted after the start Met (residue 1) and before Asn (residue 2), as decoded from the forward PCR primer (Kozak-ATG-YPYDVPDYA-NQTLNSS...) in PMC2947157. The primer sequence unambiguously encodes M(start)-HA-N(2)Q(3)T(4)L(5)N(6)S(7)S(8)..., placing the tag between residue 1 and residue 2 of the canonical sequence.

sources.claim: Human MrgD (Accession number AY427820 ) was amplified from human genomic DNA (Clontech, Palo Alto, CA) by PCR using the forward primer Xba 1 5′-CTAG TCT AGA GCC GCC ACC ATG TAC CCA TAC GAT GTT CCA GAT TAC GCT AAC CAG ACT TTG AAT AGC AGT-3′ and the reverse primer EcoR 1 5′-CCG GAA TTC TCA AGC CCC CAT CTC ATT GGT-3′.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both describe the same HA-tagged human MrgD construct from PMC2947157; L1 is used as the primary citation because it contains the primer sequence that unambiguously pins the junction to residue 1. L2 is redundant with L1 and does not add a new site. L3 and L4 describe a c-Myc-tagged rat MrgD ortholog from the same paper (PMC2947157); the rat primer encodes M-EQKLISEEDL(Myc)-NYTPYSS, placing the tag after the start Met of rat MrgD. This is indirect evidence for the same N-terminal junction in human MRGPRD, but since L1/L2 already directly validate the human protein at residue 1, L3/L4 do not add a new site and are not separately reported. The C-terminal Rluc8 fusion in L5 is intracellular (topology landmarks place residues 281-321 intracellularly) and is recorded in other_positions. ECL1 (85-99), ECL2 (164-179), and ECL3 (248-259) are not supported by any ledger line for internal tag insertion and are therefore not proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Rluc8 fusion on full-length MRGPRD (PMC12006980); the C-terminus (residues 281-321) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this is not a surface tag site.
